problem:
Arranged in **ascending order** and rounded to **the nearest integer**, the solutions of the equation $2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+1=\frac{1}{4}$ for $-{180}^{∘}<x\le {180}^{∘}$ are $x=${{field-1}}${}^{∘}$ and $x=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+1 & =\frac{1}{4} \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{3}{4} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{3}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{3}{8})=(112.024\,3…)^{∘}≈{112.024}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${112.024}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution, rounded to the nearest integer, is $x={112}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the second quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={67.976}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={67.976}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/18b8161029f2013671daadc367e54e4f02d1d7fac2134ea4953a725236cbddac.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{67.976}^{∘} \\  & ={247.976}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get a second solution that's within the required domain, we simply subtract ${360}^{∘}$ from $X:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =X-{360}^{∘} \\  & ={247.976}^{∘}-{360}^{∘} \\  & =-{112.024}^{∘} \\  & ≈-{112}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, arranged in ascending order, the solutions are $x={-112}^{∘}$ and $x={112}^{∘}.$
